message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"a19fe0de447100a9e846cb2428acc61eae22d0a5c5be1214d4978107aab9f1f2","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-co-class-std:lineage:72","source_registry_sha256":"bdc8d5a61f622fc6c91da0be8478dfb02615c007374129c91888edf82eb1b746","units":[{"unit_id":"sec10-u01","module_id":"sec10-m01","objective_ids":["sec10-u01"],"title":{"text":"Where passing is not allowed","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05","sec10-R06"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Passing needs a clear view and open space, so blocked views and busy points like crossings are off limits.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05"]},{"text":"Some passes are illegal outright, such as in a marked no-passing zone, above the speed limit, or past a stopped school bus.","fact_ids":["sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ray wants to pass a slow car just before a railroad crossing ahead.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Passing is illegal closer than one hundred feet to an intersection or a railroad crossing.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-R06"]},"result":{"text":"Ray stays behind the slow car until well past the crossing and the road ahead is clear.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking speeding up past the limit is fine as long as it is only during a pass.","fact_ids":["sec10-F03"]},"correction":{"text":"It is illegal to go over the posted speed limit while passing, just as it is illegal to pass in a marked no-passing zone.","fact_ids":["sec10-F03"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"No view, no crossing, no pass.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Ahead of you is a railroad crossing. Within what distance of it does the law forbid starting a pass?","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-R06"]},"answer":{"text":"Closer than one hundred feet.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05"]},"rationale":{"text":"The same one-hundred-foot figure applies to intersections, railroad crossings, and bridges, viaducts and tunnels with a blocked view.","fact_ids":["sec10-R06"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Places you may not pass","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Blocked views.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},{"text":"Crossings and structures.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},{"text":"Zones, speed and school buses.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"This chapter covers passing limits, hills and curves, night driving and bad weather. We begin with where you may not pass. You already know how to make a pass. Here the question is when the law says no. The list includes places where your view is blocked, places near intersections, railroad crossings, bridges, viaducts and tunnels, passing a bicyclist without enough room, marked no-passing zones, speeding while passing, and passing a stopped school bus. Each rule has the same purpose: a pass should only happen where you can see clearly and have room to finish safely.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Blocked views and structures","fact_ids":["sec10-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Hill or curve that blocks your view.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01"]},{"text":"Bridge, viaduct or tunnel with a blocked view.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01"]},{"text":"Not within one hundred feet.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Do not pass on a hill or curve that blocks your view. Do not pass within one hundred feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel when your view is blocked. The common thread is visibility. If a hill crest, a curve or a structure hides the road ahead, you cannot know whether an oncoming vehicle is about to appear. Starting a pass in that situation means gambling that the lane is empty. The handbook removes the gamble by forbidding the pass. Wait until the road opens up and you can see far enough ahead to complete the pass with room to spare.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Intersections and crossings","fact_ids":["sec10-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Not closer than one hundred feet.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05"]},{"text":"Intersections and railroad crossings.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05"]},{"text":"Bridges, curves, hills limiting view.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Passing is illegal closer than one hundred feet to an intersection or a railroad crossing, and on a bridge, curve or hill that limits what you can see. Intersections and crossings are where other road users may enter your path, or where the car you are passing may turn. A driver passing near an intersection could meet a car pulling out of a side street, or a car turning left across their path. Near a railroad crossing, a pass could leave you in the wrong lane at the tracks. Keeping one hundred feet clear of these points prevents those conflicts.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"One distance, several places","fact_ids":["sec10-R06","sec10-F01","sec10-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Intersections and railroad crossings.","fact_ids":["sec10-R06","sec10-F01","sec10-F05"]},{"text":"Bridges, viaducts and tunnels with blocked views.","fact_ids":["sec10-R06","sec10-F01","sec10-F05"]},{"text":"All one hundred feet.","fact_ids":["sec10-R06","sec10-F01","sec10-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Learners sometimes think each no-passing situation has its own distance. The no-passing distance near intersections and railroad crossings is one hundred feet, the same figure used for bridges, viaducts and tunnels with a blocked view. Questions may offer smaller or larger distances for one of these places to see whether you attach the right number. You do not need several numbers here; you need one, and the list of places it covers. If a question asks how close to any of these points you may pass, the answer is no closer than one hundred feet.","fact_ids":["sec10-R06","sec10-F01","sec10-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Other illegal passes","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Bicyclist without a three-foot buffer.","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},{"text":"Marked no-passing zone; speeding while passing.","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},{"text":"School bus with lights flashing and arm out.","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Do not pass a bicyclist unless you can keep a buffer of at least three feet, counting mirrors and other projections. A brief crossing of a solid yellow line to do so is allowed when no one is oncoming and the view ahead is clear. It is illegal to pass in a marked no-passing zone, or to go over the posted speed limit while passing. And it is illegal to pass a school bus whose red lights are flashing and whose stop arm is out. These rules do not depend on how clear the road looks. They apply every time the condition is present.","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Near a crossing","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-R06","sec10-F01","sec10-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"A railroad crossing ahead.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-R06","sec10-F01","sec10-F03"]},{"text":"How close may you pass?","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-R06","sec10-F01","sec10-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: you are behind a slow vehicle on a two-lane road, and a railroad crossing is coming up ahead. How close to the crossing is passing illegal? Decide before reading on. Passing is illegal closer than one hundred feet to a railroad crossing. The same distance applies to intersections, and to bridges, viaducts and tunnels when your view is blocked. Remember the other limits too: never pass on a hill or curve that blocks your view, in a marked no-passing zone, above the speed limit, or past a school bus with red lights flashing.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-R06","sec10-F01","sec10-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"No-passing recap","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Blocked views: no pass.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},{"text":"One hundred feet from crossings.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},{"text":"Zones, speed, buses, bicyclists.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us review. Do not pass on a hill or curve that blocks your view, or within one hundred feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel when your view is blocked. Passing is illegal closer than one hundred feet to an intersection or railroad crossing. Do not pass a bicyclist unless you can keep at least three feet of buffer, counting mirrors and projections. It is illegal to pass in a marked no-passing zone, to speed while passing, or to pass a school bus with red lights flashing and stop arm out. Next, hills and curves. Wait for a clear, legal stretch.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F05","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec10-u02","module_id":"sec10-m02","objective_ids":["sec10-u02"],"title":{"text":"Hills it.","fact_ids":["sec10-R05"]},"correction":{"text":"In a curve you slow down before entry and accelerate only after the middle, never while entering.","fact_ids":["sec10-R05","sec10-F08"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Slow in, speed out.","fact_ids":["sec10-R05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"When may you start to speed up in a crests.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08"]},{"text":"Curve speed.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Hills and curves change what you can see and how much grip your tires have. This lesson covers why they can hide hazards even on roads you know, what to do when you cannot see past the top of a hill, and how to manage your speed through a curve. The curve rule has a clear order, slowing before you enter and speeding up only after the middle, and practice questions test whether you can keep that order straight. By the end you should be able to describe how you would drive over a blind hill crest and through a sharp curve.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Hidden hazards","fact_ids":["sec10-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Hills and curves can hide hazards.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06"]},{"text":"Even on roads you know.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06"]},{"text":"Be ready to stop.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Hills and curves can hide hazards even on roads you know, so be ready to stop when one blocks your view of the road. Familiarity can work against you here. A driver who has taken the same curve every day may stop expecting anything new on the other side. But a stalled car, a fallen branch or a person walking can appear there on any day. Being ready to stop means keeping a speed at which you could stop for something you have not seen yet, and keeping your attention on the point where the road disappears from view. Look where the road disappears.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Over the crest","fact_ids":["sec10-F07","sec10-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Cannot see past the top of a hill?","fact_ids":["sec10-F07","sec10-F06"]},{"text":"Slow to a suitable speed.","fact_ids":["sec10-F07","sec10-F06"]},{"text":"Until you can see the road again.","fact_ids":["sec10-F07","sec10-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"If you cannot see past the top of a hill, slow to a suitable speed until you crest it and can see the road again. As you climb, the road beyond the top is hidden, and anything just over the crest will appear suddenly. Slowing gives you time to react once it comes into view. This rule pairs with the passing limits you just learned: you may not pass on a hill that blocks your view. So on a blind hill crest you do two things, keep right and stay behind any vehicle ahead, and slow to a speed that lets you handle what appears.","fact_ids":["sec10-F07","sec10-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Slow in, speed out","fact_ids":["sec10-R05","sec10-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Slow before entering the curve.","fact_ids":["sec10-R05","sec10-F08"]},{"text":"Accelerate only after the middle.","fact_ids":["sec10-R05","sec10-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some drivers speed up as they enter a curve, or brake hard in the middle of it. Slow down before you enter a curve, because taking it too fast lets the tires lose grip and skid. Start speeding up only after the middle of the curve. In a curve you slow down before entry and accelerate only after the middle, never while entering. Questions may describe a driver accelerating into a curve, or braking at its midpoint, and ask what went wrong. The right order is to do your slowing on the straight before the curve, then accelerate gently on the way out. Brake on the straight, not in the curve, and keep a steady speed until the middle.","fact_ids":["sec10-R05","sec10-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":49,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"When to accelerate","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R05","sec10-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Driving through a curve.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R05","sec10-F06"]},{"text":"When can you speed up?","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R05","sec10-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: you are approaching a sharp curve on a rural road. When should you slow down, and at what point may you start to speed up again? Decide before reading on. Slow down before you enter the curve, because taking it too fast lets the tires lose grip and skid. Start speeding up only after the middle of the curve, never while entering. And because curves and hills can hide hazards even on roads you know, be ready to stop for anything that appears around the bend. Keep the order: slow first, then speed up after the middle.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R05","sec10-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Hills and curves recap","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Be ready to stop.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R05"]},{"text":"Slow before a blind crest.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R05"]},{"text":"Slow in, speed out of curves.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us review. Hills and curves can hide hazards even on roads you know, so be ready to stop when one blocks your view. If you cannot see past the top of a hill, slow to a suitable speed until you crest it and can see the road again. Slow down before you enter a curve, because taking it too fast lets the tires lose grip and skid, and start speeding up only after the middle of the curve. Next, we look at driving at dawn, dusk and night, and the lighting rules that go with it. Hidden hazards, blind crests and curves all call for the same habit: a speed that lets you stop.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec10-u03","module_id":"sec10-m03","objective_ids":["sec10-u03"],"title":{"text":"Dusk, darkness and lights","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Low light limits what you and others can see, so lights and extra space reduce risk.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F17"]},{"text":"Parked cars need lights at night so others can see them, but those lights are not enough to drive by.","fact_ids":["sec10-F11","sec10-R02"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Mia pulls onto the roadside at night to check a map, then plans to drive on.","fact_ids":["sec10-F11","sec10-R02"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A parked vehicle beside the road must show parking lights from sunset to sunrise, but you may never drive on parking lights alone.","fact_ids":["sec10-F11","sec10-R02"]},"result":{"text":"Mia shows parking lights while parked, then switches to headlights before pulling back onto the road.","fact_ids":["sec10-R02","sec10-F10"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: driving at dusk with only parking lights on.","fact_ids":["sec10-R02"]},"correction":{"text":"Parking lights are required on a vehicle parked at the roadside at night, but driving with only parking lights on is not allowed.","fact_ids":["sec10-R02","sec10-F11"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Parking lights park only.","fact_ids":["sec10-R02"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Besides sunset to sunrise, what visibility condition makes headlights required by Colorado law?","fact_ids":["sec10-F10"]},"answer":{"text":"From sunset to sunrise and whenever you cannot see one thousand feet ahead.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10"]},"rationale":{"text":"Headlights are for driving; parking lights alone are only for a parked vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec10-R02","sec10-F11"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Driving in low light","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-F18"]},"lines":[{"text":"Dawn and dusk.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-F18"]},{"text":"Headlight rules.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-F18"]},{"text":"Night hazards.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-F18"]}],"narration":{"text":"Driving after dark, or in the dim light of dawn and dusk, brings risks you do not face at midday. This lesson covers why dawn and dusk can be riskier than daytime, when Colorado law requires headlights, what lights a parked car must show at the roadside, why parking lights are never enough to drive by, how to adjust your following distance at night, and which night hazards to watch for. The next lesson then covers high beams, low beams and glare. Together they give you a complete set of habits for driving when the light is poor.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-F18"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Dawn and dusk","fact_ids":["sec10-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Poor visibility.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09"]},{"text":"Small area lit by headlights.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09"]},{"text":"Glare from headlights and fog lights.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Dawn and dusk can be riskier than daytime. The handbook names three reasons: poor visibility, the small area your headlights light up, and glare from headlights combined with fog lights. Each of these reasons on its own makes hazards harder to spot, and at dawn and dusk they can all arrive together. Your headlights reach only a limited area ahead, so anything outside it stays hard to see, and glare adds to the problem. Treat these times with the same care as full darkness. Give dawn and dusk the same care you give full darkness, and keep low beams on.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Headlights and parking lights","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Headlights: sunset to sunrise.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-F11"]},{"text":"Or when you cannot see one thousand feet.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-F11"]},{"text":"Parked at the roadside: parking lights.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Colorado law requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and whenever you cannot see one thousand feet ahead. Keeping low beams or daytime running lights on all the time lowers risk. A vehicle parked beside the road, attended or not, must show parking lights from sunset to sunrise or when visibility is under one thousand feet. That lets other drivers see the parked vehicle. But never drive on parking lights alone. Parking lights do not light the road ahead well enough to drive, and they make your moving car look like a parked one to others.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Parking lights only park","fact_ids":["sec10-R02","sec10-F11","sec10-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Required when parked at night.","fact_ids":["sec10-R02","sec10-F11","sec10-F10"]},{"text":"Never used alone for driving.","fact_ids":["sec10-R02","sec10-F11","sec10-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some drivers use parking lights at dusk because they seem like a halfway step before headlights. Parking lights are required on a vehicle parked at the roadside at night, but driving with only parking lights on is not allowed. Practice questions may describe a driver at dusk using parking lights and ask whether that is acceptable. It is not. The moment the car is moving after sunset, or whenever you cannot see one thousand feet ahead, headlights are required. Parking lights belong to a parked car, which is exactly what their name says.","fact_ids":["sec10-R02","sec10-F11","sec10-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Night habits","fact_ids":["sec10-F17","sec10-F18"]},"lines":[{"text":"More following distance.","fact_ids":["sec10-F17","sec10-F18"]},{"text":"Watch for unlit vehicles and bicyclists.","fact_ids":["sec10-F17","sec10-F18"]},{"text":"Look for single headlights.","fact_ids":["sec10-F17","sec10-F18"]}],"narration":{"text":"Leave more following distance at night and on roads you do not know. With less light, you will spot hazards later, so the extra space buys back reaction time. At night, watch for vehicles and bicyclists without lights. Slow down in dark areas where people or animals may be moving. And look for the single headlight of a bicycle or a motorcycle, which can be easy to miss among the paired headlights of cars. A single light could also be a car with one headlight out, so treat any single light with care until you know what it is.","fact_ids":["sec10-F17","sec10-F18"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Headlight rules","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-R02","sec10-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"When are headlights required?","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-R02","sec10-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: on a cloudy afternoon, heavy rain cuts your view of the road ahead to well under one thousand feet. The sun has not yet set. Are headlights required? Decide before reading on. Yes. Colorado law requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and whenever you cannot see one thousand feet ahead. Parking lights alone would not be enough, because you may never drive on parking lights alone; they are for a vehicle parked at the roadside. Keeping low beams or daytime running lights on all the time lowers risk.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-R02","sec10-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Low light recap","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-R02","sec10-F17","sec10-F18"]},"lines":[{"text":"Dawn and dusk need care.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-R02","sec10-F17","sec10-F18"]},{"text":"Headlights by law; parking lights only parked.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-R02","sec10-F17","sec10-F18"]},{"text":"More space; watch for single lights.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-R02","sec10-F17","sec10-F18"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us review. Dawn and dusk can be riskier than daytime because of poor visibility, the small area your headlights light, and glare. Colorado law requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and whenever you cannot see one thousand feet ahead.
